nodes.action: Read the project guidance, current client or importer, representative input data, and external contract before editing; identify existing side effects, return shapes, and audit hooks.
nodes.name: Inspect project scope
preconditions: Target project and stated entry points are available
nodes.validator: Required files are read and the expected input, output, and dispatch boundaries are documented.

nodes.action: Translate the documented requirements into explicit local checks, including required/type/format/range/enum/normalization rules and any cross-field or duplicate constraints.
nodes.name: Derive local validation rules
nodes.validator: Every documented rejection condition has a deterministic local rule and an explicit expected representation.

nodes.action: Define one stable error object shape and a per-record failure entry that preserves the original index and payload; ensure validation accumulates all applicable field and cross-field failures before dispatch.
nodes.name: Design structured diagnostics
nodes.validator: A malformed record can yield multiple errors without terminating validation or losing its original position.

nodes.action: Update the processor to validate and normalize each record before any outbound operation, route invalid records to failures, and invoke the external operation only for records with no errors.
nodes.name: Implement pre-dispatch gate
nodes.validator: For every record, validation precedes dispatch; records with errors produce no outbound call, while valid records retain input order.

nodes.action: Return the project’s required aggregate structure with complete successes, failures, trace or audit data when applicable, and totals derived from the original batch rather than hard-coded counts.
nodes.name: Preserve batch accounting
nodes.validator: Total equals succeeded plus failed, every input index appears exactly once, and failure details retain original values where required.

nodes.action: Exercise valid records, each individual invalid condition, combinations of simultaneous failures, optional fields, timezone or normalization boundaries when relevant, duplicates, and mixed batches.
nodes.name: Build boundary-focused checks
nodes.validator: Checks cover both rejection semantics and the absence of outbound calls for rejected records.

nodes.action: Run the focused checks and inspect returned structures plus the mock or audit trace; compare observed calls, indices, errors, normalized values, and counts against the derived contract.
nodes.name: Run verification first
nodes.validator: All checks pass, invalid records have no dispatch trace, valid records are dispatched, and diagnostics are complete and contract-shaped.

nodes.action: Read the project guidance, current implementation, input shape, and authoritative reference material; identify required outputs, validation rules, normalization policies, and side-effect boundaries.
nodes.name: Discover authoritative contract
preconditions: Project files and task inputs are available
nodes.validator: Required fields, optional fields, accepted values, error schema, and output schema are recorded without relying on remote responses.

nodes.action: Trace the current control flow and identify where malformed data can reach external effects, where processing stops early, and which observability hooks can prove behavior.
nodes.name: Inspect baseline behavior
nodes.validator: Every requested behavior has a corresponding observable verification point.

nodes.action: Create or select a deterministic projection that preserves original records and indices while making types, defaults, canonical values, and comparison forms explicit.
nodes.name: Define normalized local representation
nodes.validator: Optional inputs remain optional, defaults are explicit, and normalized values are suitable for all contract comparisons.

nodes.action: Evaluate every applicable rule for each record before dispatch, accumulate all failures for a record, and classify each record as accepted or rejected with structured field-level diagnostics.
nodes.name: Screen records completely
outputs: Rejected records with complete error lists
nodes.validator: Invalid records contain all discovered failures in the required consistent shape; valid records contain no screening errors.

nodes.action: Invoke the external operation only for accepted candidates, preserving input order and isolating rejected records from side effects.
nodes.name: Dispatch accepted records
nodes.validator: Dispatch trace contains no rejected record and successful count matches the number of accepted candidates.

nodes.action: Build the requested return object with successes, failures, original indices or records, normalized evidence where required, trace data, and aggregate counts.
nodes.name: Assemble structured result
nodes.validator: Result keys, nested error fields, ordering, and summary counts match the discovered contract.

nodes.action: Run focused checks covering valid processing, multiple simultaneous failures, optional/default behavior, boundary and normalization cases, ordering, and no-dispatch guarantees; inspect the diff for scope compliance.
nodes.name: Verify final artifact
outputs: Evidence of local rejection and correct dispatch
preconditions: Implementation changes are saved in the required project directory
nodes.validator: All required scenarios pass, invalid inputs never trigger outbound calls, valid inputs still progress, and no unrelated project relocation or stub replacement occurred.
